name: Forms
summary: What a form control is, and how every form control is labelled, described, marked as required and validated, and how a form reports its errors, on every platform.
description: A form control is a component through which people enter or choose a value the product keeps, whether or not it sits in a form that is submitted. Each control is specified on its own page; this foundation says which components are form controls and holds what they share, so that a field behaves the same way next to its neighbours and on every platform: its anatomy (label, description, message), how a required field is marked, which validation statuses exist and how they render, when a value is checked, how errors are announced and summarised, and how fields are spaced. Draft: the rules below describe what the controls do today and what every trusted source agrees on; each open point is decided one step at a time with the team.

rules.name: What a form control is
rules.text: A form control is a component through which people enter or choose a value the product keeps: text, a number, one or several options, on or off, a point in a range. It has a visible label and may have a description; when its value can be missing or wrong, it can be marked required and report an error. Whether the value applies at once or with the rest of the form depends on how the control is used, not on the component.

rules.name: Which rules a control follows
rules.text: Every form control follows the rules on its anatomy and its label. A control that can be marked required also follows the rules on required fields, and a control that can show a severity (it has the severity property, or the error state it sets) also follows the rules on severities, errors and their announcement. Which rules a control follows is read from its specification: its label part, its required property, its severity property and its message part, with no list of exceptions. Not decided yet (step 2b): whether the Search field, which can be required but has no severity, gets one, and whether the label, required and message guidelines the controls repeat move into this foundation.

rules.name: Form actions
rules.text: A button that submits a form is a form action, not a form control: people activate it, they do not enter or choose a value with it. It does not follow this foundation as a control; the rules about the actions of a form name it in their text.

rules.name: Anatomy of a field
rules.text: A field stacks a visible label, the control, an optional description (format, example, constraint) and, when it shows a severity, a message saying what is wrong and how to fix it, what to check or what was confirmed. A group of checkboxes or radios takes the same parts around its options, with a legend as its label. Today the message is shown under the description; whether it replaces it is not decided yet.

rules.name: Label
rules.text: Every control has a visible label that stays visible while people type, associated with the control so assistive technology announces it as the control's name. A placeholder is never the label.

rules.name: Required fields
rules.text: A required field is exposed as required to assistive technology and marked visibly before people submit, never by color alone. Today the words are left to the author (in the label or the description) and no mark is drawn; the mark itself is not decided yet.

rules.name: Severities
rules.text: A form control can show one of three severities, none by default: an error says the value is not accepted and how to fix it, a warning says the value is accepted but deserves attention, a success says the value was checked and confirmed. The word is "error", not "invalid": every platform's guidance speaks of errors (WCAG 3.3.1 Error Identification, the Compose error semantics, Material's error text), while invalid is the web's technical term. There is no information severity: information that holds before any check is the description's job, and no source gives a field an information status. The property is severity, and one message carries every severity. The Checkbox, the Checkbox group and the Radio group have only the error severity: a choice has nothing to confirm or to warn about (our judgment, not a source's). On the web, the error is aria-invalid="true" (and :user-invalid when the browser validates); a warning and a success have no web state, since aria-invalid has no value for them: they are the message text and the styling. The control's border takes the severity's accent functional border color and the message its functional text color. Since the Color foundation 7.1.0 (decision border-accent-functional-3-to-1) the accent borders reach the 3:1 of WCAG 1.4.11 on every surface level; the one shortfall left is the light warning border on the subtle warning fill (2.95:1), which step 6 may use as the fill, accepted knowingly by the team (issue #119).

rules.name: Severity in the fill
rules.text: Validated, rendered in step 6: the severity is also shown in the control's fill, a solid color, never translucent; perhaps the subtle functional background of the severity (to confirm).

rules.name: Severity icon
rules.text: Validated, rendered in step 6: the severity icon is never drawn inside the area where people type, because browsers add their own elements there (autofill, password manager, reveal, clear, spin and picker controls). It goes after the control, or at the start of the message, or nowhere, and then the message says the severity ("Error: …", "Warning: …", "Success: …"). It appears in one place only, never both after the control and in the message.

rules.name: Width without the icon
rules.text: Validated, rendered in step 6: without the icon after the control, the control keeps its default width and takes the whole width; the place after the control is not reserved.

rules.name: A severity is said in text
rules.text: An error is identified in text next to the control it concerns, associated with that control, and never shown by color alone. The text says what is wrong and, when a fix is known, how to fix it. A warning and a success are said in text the same way, whatever icon or color accompanies them.

rules.name: When a value is checked
rules.text: Not decided yet: on submit, when people leave the field, or as they type. A control is never marked as in error before validation ran.

rules.name: How errors are announced
rules.text: Not decided yet, for each platform: where focus goes after a failed submit, and how an error that appears without a submit reaches assistive technology.

rules.name: Error summary
rules.text: Not decided yet: whether a form lists its errors above the fields, with a link to each field.

rules.name: Spacing
rules.text: Not decided yet: the space between fields, between groups of fields and before the form's actions. Today a field spaces its own parts by its container gap, and a group by its row gap.

rules.name: Web rendering
rules.text: A label element pointing at the control's id; the description and the message referenced by aria-describedby for every severity; the required attribute on a required control; aria-invalid="true" on a control in error and only then; data-severity on the component for the three severities; a fieldset and its legend around a group of checkboxes or radios.

contrast.description: The message of an error on every surface level. Measured only while the severities are being rendered (WCAG 1.4.3 asks 4.5:1).
The message of a warning on every surface level. Measured only (WCAG 1.4.3 asks 4.5:1).
The message of a success on every surface level. Measured only (WCAG 1.4.3 asks 4.5:1).

The border that identifies a control in error, the accent functional border. Measured only (WCAG 1.4.11 asks 3:1): 6.12 / 5.79 / 6.12 / 5.79:1 in light mode and 4.97 / 4.55 / 4.16 / 3.73:1 in dark mode on levels 0 to 3, since the Color foundation 7.1.0.

The border of a control with a warning, the accent functional border. Measured only (WCAG 1.4.11 asks 3:1): 3.27 / 3.09 / 3.27 / 3.09:1 in light mode and 8.09 / 7.41 / 6.78 / 6.07:1 in dark mode on levels 0 to 3, since the Color foundation 7.1.0. On the subtle warning fill it is 2.95:1 in light mode, a shortfall the team accepted knowingly (issue #119).
The border of a control with a success, the accent functional border. Measured only (WCAG 1.4.11 asks 3:1).

guidelines.text: A control through which people enter or choose a value has a visible label or instructions whether or not it sits in a form that is submitted; a link or a control not associated with data entry does not.
Activating a button that submits a form is not changing the setting of a control: entering text, checking a box or choosing an option in a list is, and does not submit the form by itself.
A button contributes to the submitted data only when it is the one that submitted the form.
A form either applies each value at once (a settings page) or collects the values and applies them when people choose to submit; the same input controls serve both.
On macOS, a switch can sit in a grouped form, where a mini switch controls the setting of a single row.
Every control has a visible label or instructions, associated with it programmatically.
Related controls are grouped, and the group has a name: a set of radios always, a set of checkboxes or related fields when it helps.
A required field is indicated visibly, not only programmatically and never by color alone; a symbol used to mark it is explained before its first use.
When an input error is detected, the field in error is identified and the error is described in text; color or an icon may add to the text, never replace it.
A warning and a success are said in text like an error, never by color or an icon alone, and a confirmation that appears without moving focus is exposed as a status message.
Set aria-invalid="true" for an error only: it has no value for a warning or a success, which the message text says.
When a correction is known, the error message suggests it, unless that would jeopardize the security or purpose of the content.
A control is marked as in error only after its value was validated, not before people used it.
A message that reports errors or a result without moving focus, such as the number of errors in a form, is exposed as a status message so assistive technology announces it.
Validate fields when it makes sense: an email address when people move to another field, a user name or password before they leave it; show errors right next to the field.
Make sure people understand that they must provide the required data before they can continue, for example by enabling the Next or Continue button only once the required fields are filled in.
Expose an error with the error semantics of the field, so the screen reader reads the error with it; announce content that changes without focus with a polite live region.
Error identification, labels or instructions and error suggestion apply to non-web software as they do to web content.

decisions.text: Form controls can show three severities, error, warning and success, set by the severity property (none, error, warning, success; none by default) with one message for every severity. The Text field, the Number field, the Textarea and the Select take all four values; the Checkbox, the Checkbox group and the Radio group take none and error only (our judgment, not a source's). The property and the state invalid and errorMessage are removed, with no alias: the packages are alpha and unreleased, so a clean break (a major change of the specs, 0.x minor). The severity border is the accent functional border, global.border.accent.functional.<severity>.default, and the message color the functional text color, global.text.on-base.functional.<severity>.default. On the web the error is aria-invalid="true" and the severity data-severity; a warning and a success are text and styling only. The accent borders were under 3:1 (the light warning one at 2.13:1 down to 2.01:1, the dark error one, which had no dark value, at 2.82:1 down to 2.11:1), and the team fixed them in the Color foundation 7.1.0 (decision border-accent-functional-3-to-1): warning 500 in light mode, error 400 in dark mode, 3:1 or more on every surface level; the one shortfall left is the light warning border on the subtle warning fill (2.95:1, which step 6 may use as the fill), accepted knowingly by the team (issue #119). Validated, to render in step 6: the severity in the fill, a solid color; the severity icon never inside the typing area, in one place only (after the control, at the start of the message, or nowhere, then the message says the severity); the control keeping its default width without the icon after it.
decisions.rationale: Options. A: errors only, as Apple and Material do (no source for the other two on a field). B: every status (error, warning, success, information), as Fluent does. C: keep invalid and add a separate status property, two properties for one thing. D: errors and success, as the W3C does (a success confirmation with icon and text). The team validated three severities (B without information, which the description covers; W3C confirms a success, only Fluent has a warning). Name: severity was chosen over status (it clashes with the spec's status and with WCAG status messages), intent (it means a destructive action on the Button) and validation; component libraries and developers use severity for success, danger and warning alerts, even if it is odd for success. "Error" over "invalid": the platforms say error (WCAG 3.3.1, Compose error semantics, Material text fields guidelines and accessibility), and invalid is the web's technical term (aria-invalid, :invalid, :user-invalid); Understanding 4.1.3 and the Windows Forms page still use invalid as an adjective of the value. The accent border (rather than the base one) was the team's correction. Sources opened: WCAG Understanding 3.3.1, 3.3.3, 4.1.3, 1.4.1, 1.4.11 and 1.1.1, ARIA21, the WAI notifications tutorial, MDN aria-invalid and :invalid, Apple HIG Writing, Feedback, Text fields and Entering data, Compose semantics, Material text fields guidelines and accessibility, Windows Forms, Text box and LiveSetting.

decisions.text: A form control is a component through which people enter or choose a value the product keeps (text, a number, one or several options, on or off, a point in a range); it has a visible label and may have a description, and when its value can be missing or wrong it can be marked required and report an error. Whether the value applies at once or with the rest of the form depends on how the control is used, not on the component. A button that submits is a form action, not a form control. The components that follow the foundation are the ones whose role profile is marked as input (roles.json), read from each specification: the rules on anatomy and label for every input, on required fields for those with a required property, on validation for those with the invalid state.
decisions.rationale: Labels and instructions are not limited to forms (WCAG 3.3.2), a submit button is activating a control, not changing a setting (WCAG 3.2.2), and Windows tells instantly updating forms from submitting ones, so a control is defined by what people do with it, not by where it sits. The role profiles already name the roles that require WCAG 3.3.2, so the foundation reads them (input) instead of keeping a list. Also considered: a section in each specification declaring when its value applies (at once or on submit), which writes a web submit model into specifications iOS and Android have no source for; a scope per rule, the most precise and the most work; an explicit list of identifiers, which silently leaves a new component out. Known weak spot: the role group is generic, so a future component with the role group that is not an input would be counted as one; revisit it then. Known gap, set aside until the complex controls are aligned after the Text field: the Checkbox has the invalid state and no error message part (the validator warns).

decisions.text: Material's component guidelines (m3.material.io/components/) and Microsoft's Windows app controls guidance and WinUI automation reference are trusted sources, so the form rules for Android and Windows cite those platforms' own guidance.
decisions.rationale: They hold the only Android and Windows guidance on forms (required marking, error text replacing the supporting text, spacing, announcing changes); without them, the foundation could only say these platforms are silent.

changelog.note: Breaking, decision forms-validation-severities: the invalid status is replaced by three severities, error, warning and success (the severity property, one message for all); the rule on statuses becomes the rule on severities, with the web mapping and the validated rules on the fill, the icon and the width (rendered in step 6); the tiers read the severity property; the measured status borders read the accent functional border. The examples use severity and message, with a warning and a success of the Text field.

A form control is defined by what people do with it, and the foundation applies to every component whose role profile is marked as input; a button that submits is a form action (forms-input-components).
Material's component guidelines and Microsoft's Windows app controls guidance become trusted sources for the form rules on Android and Windows (forms-platform-sources).

First draft of the page, to show how the foundation will be represented: rules describing what the form controls do today and what every trusted source agrees on, the open points named as not decided, the status colors measured on every surface level without a minimum while the statuses are decided. No decision yet.
